summary: The decision DB-013 declined to take from a security fix, taken under CP-102: which roles carry workforce.view and workforce.manage in org_role_permissions, how they are provisioned, and what a department manager receives. The decision is a RULE derived from the live capability catalog, not a transcribed table, so it cannot drift from lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts. WFC-003 specifies the migration; WFC-004 writes it. WFC-003 authored no SQL.

the_problem_measured.what: org_role_permissions is the ONLY authority the workforce RLS policies read, via has_perm(uid, org_id, perm) (20260821180438:122-151). It is seeded with five roles across two migrations (20250816132000:44-49 and 20260712005429:219-235) and NONE of them carries any workforce.* permission. Re-derived independently by WFC-003 from the chain, not taken on DB-013's word.
the_problem_measured.consequence: Split-brain authorization, and a silent one. lib/auth/admin-context.ts:222-243 loadCapabilities() passes BOTH org_role_permissions.perms AND the role string into resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilities, which UNIONS them (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:464-480). So an org administrator passes withAdminCapability('workforce.manage') on the TypeScript catalog alone, the route admits the caller, and then staff_members_scoped_read evaluates has_perm(...,'workforce.view') OR has_perm(...,'workforce.manage') against a matrix that grants neither, so the policy denies and the caller receives ZERO ROWS.
the_problem_measured.why_rls_really_applies: Admin API routes use a user-scoped client, not a service client: withAdminCapability -> withAuth -> authenticateApiRequest -> createServerClient (lib/auth/api-auth.ts:143,276-292). createServiceClient exists in that file but is only used inside checkAdminPermissions for a gate check and is never handed to a route.
the_problem_measured.blast_radius: 20+ live route handlers gated on workforce.view / workforce.manage (app/api/admin/workforce/people, app/api/admin/staff, app/api/admin/team-members, app/api/admin/tours/teams, app/api/admin/tours/team-members, app/api/admin/users/search, app/api/admin/onboarding/workflows/advance, app/api/admin/staff-operations/*, app/api/tours/[id]/team, app/api/events/[id]/staff, and others) and 20+ live readers of staff_members. The empty result is exactly the CP-098 hazard: a plausible zero reporting no coverage, no absences and no payroll exposure.
the_problem_measured.vocabulary_mismatch: The chain seeds 5 roles; ROLE_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:123-138) defines 12. department_manager, viewer, worker, ticketing, ticketing_manager, finance_manager and production_manager have NO org_role_permissions row at all, and has_perm returns false for EVERY permission when the row is missing (20260821180438:139, `if member_role is null then return false`). That is a wider availability problem than the workforce one; this handoff decides the workforce slice only.

the_decision.rule_not_table: deriveWorkforceRoleSeedDecisions in types/vendor-identity-contract.ts computes seed(role) = { c in workforce.* INTERSECT catalog(role) : c is NOT department-scoped }. The subtraction is the whole decision. The test asserts the derived answer against the live catalog, so an ADMIN-012 change to any role's capabilities turns this suite red until WFC-003 re-decides.
the_decision.why_has_perm_cannot_carry_a_department_s: has_perm(uid, oid, perm) has no target argument. Any permission present in org_role_permissions is therefore granted across the ENTIRE organization. Putting workforce.manage there for department_manager would hand a department manager organization-wide management authority, which is precisely what CP-094 forbids and precisely what ADMIN-012 removed from the resolver at :481-487. Withholding is the posture, not an oversight.

per_role.why: CP-094: organization administrators retain organization-wide workforce authority. Already carries the superseded staff.manage (20250816132000:45), which is retained.
Same CP-094 sentence. admin is the seeded organization administrator and already carries staff.manage (20250816132000:46), retained.
Catalog grants all three; the role already has a matrix row.
PRODUCTION_CAPABILITIES is TOUR_MANAGER minus tour.archive/tour.publish/hiring.manage, so workforce.manage survives.
Same catalog slice as production; currently has NO matrix row, so this is a new row.
FINANCE_CAPABILITIES is OPERATIONS_VIEW plus finance/contract, and OPERATIONS_VIEW contains workforce.view.
Same catalog slice as finance; currently NO matrix row.

workforce.manage is department-scoped in the resolver and has_perm cannot express that, so seeding it would be an organization-wide grant. workforce.view is org-wide at the RLS layer; that residual belongs to WFC-005/WFC-006, not to this decision.
Empty capability set by design. Workers read their own row through staff_members_worker_read_own (20260926150000:259-264).

the_decision.organization_administrator_default: org_role_permissions rows for owner and admin carry workforce.view, workforce.manage and workforce.publish, organization-wide. staff.manage is retained, not removed. Additive only.
the_decision.department_manager_default: org_role_permissions row for department_manager carries workforce.view and workforce.publish and DELIBERATELY NOT workforce.manage.

provisioning_mechanism.answer: MIGRATION, authored by WFC-004, applied under CP-051 manual additive apply. Forward-only, one transaction, no supabase db reset, no blanket replay.
why_not_configuration: roleperms_select ... using (true) (20250816132000:112) makes the matrix WORLD-READABLE, so a tenant-configurable role matrix is a public configuration surface.

The matrix decides RLS. A per-tenant matrix means the grant set differs per organization, which is the CP-104 hazard at a new site: 'the chain says X' and 'the target has X' stop being the same claim. DB-002 already established that migrations have been applied out of band through the Management API.
Role defaults are a product contract, not tenant data, so they belong in the chain where a replay reproduces them.
provisioning_mechanism.what_stays_configuration: Per-TENANT delegation. The split is deliberate: the DEFAULT role matrix is schema, the DEVIATION from it is tenant data. The existing mechanism is the per-member org_members.permissions array, already constrained to the capability catalog by org_members_permissions_check (20260821180438:81-96) and unioned by has_perm (same file:143-149). Do not invent a second one.
provisioning_mechanism.operational_consequence: admin_acting_context_sessions.capability_version is encode(digest(concat_ws('|', v_role, array_to_string(v_perms, ',')), 'sha256')) (20260722002848:171) and the same expression is re-checked on every use (:302). Mutating a role's perms therefore INVALIDATES EVERY ACTIVE ACTING-CONTEXT SESSION for members of that role. Land all roles in ONE migration so a single re-activation covers it, and verify the re-activation path BEFORE applying.

gap_or_posture.genuine_gap: owner, admin, tour_manager, production, production_manager, finance, finance_manager, viewer. The catalog grants the capability, the route admits the caller, the database returns nothing. Closes when WFC-004's migration lands.
gap_or_posture.deliberate_posture: department_manager. The authority is real, resource-scoped, and unsatisfiable until WFC-004 creates the department entity and a department-scoped policy. Recorded so nobody 'fixes' it by widening the matrix, which is the one change that would actually violate CP-094.
gap_or_posture.not_changed_here: isOrganizationCreator / isMasterAccount return ALL_CAPABILITIES in the resolver (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:462) but bypass has_perm entirely, so a creator or master with no org_members row is authorized at the route and still reads nothing. The correct remedy is a membership row, not a new RLS bypass.

what_wfc_004_must_write.one_migration: A single forward-only migration under CP-051 that upserts org_role_permissions for all twelve ROLE_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES roles with the workforce.* slice above, ADDITIVE (no removals; staff.manage stays).
what_wfc_004_must_write.required_post_condition_inside_the_trans: For every role in ROLE_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES, assert seeded(perms INTERSECT 'workforce.*') equals the workforce slice resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilities returns for that role with NO target and NO departmentAuthority. Raise exception on mismatch. This is the same rule WFC-003's test derives, so it is checkable on both sides of the migration and it is what stops the two vocabularies drifting again. Style reference: 20260926150000:273-361.
do_not: Do not add workforce.manage to department_manager. That is the one change that turns a deliberate posture into a CP-094 violation.
Do not remove staff.manage or any existing permission. Additive only.
Do not add a second membership or role table, and do not introduce a new permission vocabulary. has_perm + org_members + org_role_permissions is the whole model.

Do not create a department table in this migration. WFC-004's department entity is contract section 6 item 5 and is a separate migration; if it lands first, the department-scoped RLS path can be built in the same series, but workforce.manage still must not go in the role matrix.
Do not treat free-text staff_members.department or employment_assignments.department as a department scope.
what_wfc_004_must_write.if_wfc_004_prefers_configuration: Then the decision above does not hold, because the matrix is world-readable and a per-tenant matrix changes the RLS grant set per organization. In that case the correct move is a new CP, not a local choice, and WFC-003 must be the CP's author.

residual_gaps_named: The non-workforce permissions the seven matrix-less roles lose are a SEPARATE question this contract does not answer. Seeding only the workforce.* slice leaves viewer unable to read tours, events, logistics, finance, ticketing, site_map and content through RLS, exactly as it is today. WFC-004 may widen the seed to the full catalog projection; that is a new decision and belongs in a new CP authored by WFC-003.

workforce.view is organization-wide at the RLS layer for every role, including department_manager. CP-094's sentence is about management authority; ADMIN-012 deliberately left workforce.view unscoped (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:307-313). Reconciling the RLS read path with CP-094 is WFC-005/WFC-006's.
workforce.publish is department-unscoped by ADMIN-012's explicit decision, so seeding it for department_manager is org-wide. Same owner, same reason.
isOrganizationCreator / isMasterAccount bypass has_perm entirely. Unchanged, and deliberately not changed by this decision.
